issues.legal_issue: A civil eviction suit validly instituted before rent-control protections are extended to the area may be decided by the civil court after the extension, and a resulting decree remains executable unless the legislation provides otherwise for pending suits or decrees.
material_facts: The landlord filed a civil suit for possession while the premises were outside the area covered by the rent-control legislation, after terminating the tenancy.
While the suit was pending, a notification extended the rent-control legislation to the area.
The civil court passed a possession decree after that extension.

The legislation gave the Rent Tribunal jurisdiction over landlord-tenant disputes in covered areas but contained no provision barring decision of pending civil suits or execution of decrees in those suits.
issues.conclusion: The civil court could validly pass the decree after the legislation became applicable to the area, and the decree remains executable. The appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 1(2) and 18 of the Rajasthan Rent Control Act, 2001, the Act applies to areas from the effective date of the relevant notification, and the Rent Tribunal has jurisdiction over landlord-tenant disputes in areas to which the Act extends. Section 18 does not invalidate or transfer suits already validly instituted in civil court. In the absence of an express or implied provision applying the new regime to pending suits or barring execution of decrees in them, the law applicable when the suit was instituted governs it, and the parties’ rights crystallise on that date. This approach is supported by Nand Kishore Marwah v. Samundri Devi, Ramesh Chandra v. III Additional District Judge, Atma Ram Mittal v. Ishwar Singh Punia, Shri Kishan v. Manoj Kumar, Mansoor Khan v. Motiram Harebhan Kharat, and Rajender Bansal v. Bhuru; Vineet Kumar v. Mangal Sain Wadhera was specifically held not to be good law in Shri Kishan. The Court distinguished statutory schemes that expressly restrict execution of earlier decrees, including Section 13 of the East Punjab Rent Restriction Act, 1949.

rule.if: civil_eviction_suit and suit_valid_when_filed and rent_protection_extended_during_suit and later_decree_passed and not pending_case_or_decree_bar

predicates.civil_eviction_suit: A landlord brought a civil-court suit seeking eviction of a tenant from rented premises.
predicates.suit_valid_when_filed: The civil court had jurisdiction when the landlord instituted the suit under the law then applicable to the premises.
predicates.rent_protection_extended_during_suit: Rent-control protections were extended to the area while the civil suit was pending.
predicates.later_decree_passed: The civil court passed an eviction decree after those protections were extended to the area.
predicates.pending_case_or_decree_bar: The legislation expressly or impliedly bars the civil court from deciding the pending suit or bars execution of a decree in such a suit.
predicates.decree_remains_valid_and_executable: The civil-court eviction decree remains legally valid and may be executed.

issues.definition: When a landlord validly brings a civil eviction suit before rent-control protections extend to the area, and those protections do not bar pending suits or decrees, a decree later passed in the suit remains valid and executable.

issues.legal_issue: A court may decide an appeal raising a legal question that is also pending in other cases without waiting to hear those cases together.
material_facts: The appellants asked for their appeals to be heard with pending cases involving the same or similar legal question.
The pending cases had been brought on behalf of landlords, while the present appeals had been brought by tenants seeking to remain in possession.
The Court considered that it could answer the legal question in the appeals before it.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to defer the appeals or hear them together with the pending cases, and proceeded to decide the legal question.
issues.legal_principle: Although cases raising the same or similar questions are ideally heard together, there is no bar to deciding a case before the Court. Once the legal question is answered in one matter, other pending matters can follow that answer; the Court also considered the materially different interests represented in the respective cases.

predicates.appeal_presented: A party brought an appeal before the court for decision.
predicates.similar_question_pending_elsewhere: Other pending cases raise the same or a similar legal question.
predicates.present_appeal_and_pending_cases_involve: The parties bringing the appeal and the parties in the related pending cases have materially different interests.
predicates.court_may_decide_appeal_without_waiting_: The court may decide the appeal without first hearing it together with the related pending cases.

issues.definition: When an appeal presents a question also pending elsewhere, and the cases involve materially different interests, the court may decide the appeal without waiting for the related cases.
